items.title: The three magically-sealed chests from the Hound of Cassel raid — Liège–Scarem Montem cipher letters.
items.context:
Legal status is a deliberately fuzzy area; the covenant decided to hold them "for now," prepared to return them if Scarem Montem comes asking. Never revisited since. (Worth noting: Normandy Tribunal custom holds it's legal to raid non-magical items from another covenant — part of why keeping the chests was even a live option rather than an obvious violation.)

Update (2026-07-25) — GM: still unexplored; contents NOT yet defined. To be figured out once the open-questions backlog pass is complete (flagged for end-of-pass follow-up, alongside t032). Includes deciding the wrinkle: do the chests return with the Hound of Cassel (now going back to Scarem Montem under Wilhelm, t002), get kept/opened first, or become their own negotiation. Kept Open.

CONTENTS DEFINED (2026-08-08, developing q027 #6). The three chests hold MISSIVES from the BISHOPRIC OF LIÈGE to SCAREM MONTEM — correspondence in which Scarem Montem is exploring a similar SUBORNING OF CHURCH OR STATE, a wild violation of the Code of Hermes (interfering with the mundanes / meddling with the Church). Liège being a prince-bishopric adjacent to Brabant, this ties directly into the existing conspiracy web: the Duke-of-Brabant / Church infiltration (t028 Reynald de Grimbergen, c023, t027) and the Lotharingian-Tribunal manoeuvring (t010, t017). The letters were intercepted IN TRANSIT (Summer 1221 piracy) and never reached their recipient.

THE CIPHER — magical public/private-key cryptography via MATCHED RINGS. Each correspondent holds a pair. Enclosed WITH each letter is a ring that functions as the SENDER'S PUBLIC KEY: the recipient wears it to VERIFY WHO WROTE the letter (an unforgeable signature). The recipient's OWN ring is their PRIVATE KEY: it DECRYPTS letters that were written to them — but only letters the sender composed while holding that recipient's public-key ring, so that only the matching private ring can read them. Reading a letter thus needs BOTH: the enclosed sender-ring (to verify) and the intended recipient's private ring (to decrypt).

WHAT THE COVENANT ACTUALLY HAS: the letters plus the enclosed LIÈGE (sender) public-key rings — but NOT Scarem Montem's PRIVATE rings, which stayed with the intended recipient. Consequence: they can VERIFY authorship and so hold UNASSAILABLE PROOF OF AT LEAST ONE PARTY — that the Bishopric of Liège was corresponding with Scarem Montem, and which Liège hands signed — even though they generally CANNOT read the ciphertext itself. Getting plaintext would require capturing Scarem Montem's private ring, coercing a decrypt, or a hard magical break (Intellego Vim / Mentem against a cipher likely built so only the intended mind can read). The rings are themselves magical items now in the covenant's possession.

THE SCENE-6 WRINKLE: these chests are Scarem Montem's own property, riding Scarem Montem's own stolen hull (the Hound of Cassel), which WILHELM is now sailing back to Scarem Montem to settle the ship-for-book/thesis debt (t002). So Wilhelm may be about to hand Scarem Montem back the very (mostly-unreadable) evidence that proves them guilty of a hanging-level Code violation — unless he realises what he carries and keeps it as leverage in the swap, or turns it over to the Tribunal / the Brabant-conspiracy investigators. Open: does Wilhelm know what's in the hold, and does he return, keep, or weaponise it? Kept Open.

MOTIVE LINK (2026-08-08): this is a hidden cause of Scarem Montem's rushed TRIBUNAL ESCALATION. Their incriminating Liège correspondence went missing with the pirated ship (the Hound of Cassel) and they never learned what became of it — so, unable to risk their Church/State-suborning plans being exposed and not knowing who held the evidence, they FORCED THE PACE at the 1223 Normandy Tribunal (see verified event 'Scarem Montem steals the Tapestry and declares for Lotharingia', 1223-06-26, and Bridget's Lotharingian pitch, t010): moving openly for Lotharingia and seizing the Tapestry rather than playing the long game. In hindsight their haste reads as a tell — they were running scared of exactly what is sitting in these three chests. The covenant still doesn't know it holds the leash.

Update (2026-08-08 session): Found and secured. Wilhelm discovered the three sealed boxes aboard the Hound of Cassel (his new ship) at the Isle of Man. They remain magically sealed and UNOPENED in-fiction (the Liège-cipher content above is GM prep, not yet revealed). Legal status: taken in Valdemar's raid on a Scarem Montem vessel; magical goods are protected by the Code, so they were held in trust and never returned — now awkward since Scarem Montem left the Tribunal. items.title: Wilhelm's plan to turn folk magic into a real "pocket" magic system.
items.context:
Player's stated research roadmap: (1) mine Hermetic texts — probably a Root or two — for hedge-magic inspiration; (2) turn that into actual Insight, ideally as ceremonial spells folk wizards can learn; (3) send the research assistants out into Ireland to gather more raw material; (4) fold the results back into the folk-magic system properly, which needs formulaic spellcasting (no more halving rolls to cast), ceremonial casting (adding Aura + Philosophiae), and — as a bonus, since folk magic already uses them informally — a correct integration of props. Basic enchanting (already loosely possible via Magic Lore + vis) is flagged as a later, incremental step. Player's own assessment: the first three are "REALLY EASY" to incorporate — the Learned Magicians seem to have worked out parts of it already without any Magic Theory at all.

Update (2026-07-25) — GM: follow-up needed, but BLOCKED on a resource dependency — the GM is converting the relevant hedge/folk-magic sourcebooks into the titterpig DSL format; revisit once those are in-hand. Core-rules scaffolding is already documented at integrating_magic.html (folk magic = Major Breakthrough via the Insight/Integration track → Supernatural Virtues); the converted supplements will supply the specific hedge-tradition content and settle the q017 rider (further-guideline progression within an already-initiated branch). Keep Open, awaiting resources.

IN-FICTION PROGRESS (session 2026-07-25, proposed_events p047/p049/p050): the roadmap is being narrated forward even while the mechanics stay blocked. Wilhelm's winter at Carrick (p049) cracked step (4)'s core — the FORMULAIC-RITUAL integration that drops the divide-by-two and lets a folk caster add Artes Liberales + Philosophiae (he judged it 'really easy — someone just needed to point it out'); the remaining labor is formalizing the Artes-Liberales/Philosophiae contribution (geometry to draw a true circle, rhetoric to project words of power). Step (3) is underway — assistants sent west/south, paid in grain and silver. Step (1)/(2) fed by the augury insight (environmental/contextual magic, p047) and by actually TEACHING the folk basics to a púca (p050). Narrative momentum is real; the mechanical write-up still waits on the sourcebook→DSL conversion.

COMPLICATION SURFACED (session prep 2026-08-08, developing q027 #1): the system's first CONFIRMED, method-attributable failure mode. Wilhelm's test cases so far have been tiny (his research staff, the púca Brussel, the boy Rody). Once the assistants take the 'easy stuff' out to VOLUME over the winter (paid in grain and silver, p049), the sample finally gets large enough for the failure rate to show — and the failure is not a fizzle but MADNESS: taught subjects going completely mind-broken, more likely the harder the working is pushed. The GM's frame: the Gift normally shields a caster from the backlash of channelling magic (the road to Twilight); the ungifted have no such buffer, so pushing raw magic through them comes due as insanity with no Twilight to cash it out safely — a clean magnitude dial (low-magnitude folk effects broadly safe, risk climbing with how hard it's pushed). The magic still WORKS; what it lacks is a safety margin. Whether this is a flaw in Wilhelm's specific formalization or an inherent property of ungifted magic is itself unsettled — see the new q028. This does not sink the thesis (the brass acorn, t071, quietly attests Wilhelm has a future far enough out to keep at it) but it reshapes it.

MECHANICS RULING (session 2026-06-20) — how the un-Gifted LEARN and USE this. Settled at the table: a mundane learns folk magic either by (a) original research (the only path for the very first practitioner, since no one could have initiated them), or (b) INITIATION — where the initiation Ability is MAGIC LORE, which doubles as the casting Ability (as with the Forest-path ability in the core book). Magic Theory is NOT required to initiate, but IS required to harvest vis and to give general laboratory aid. Trade-off flagged: harvesting vis on Magic Theory alone rounds up to ~2 pawns/season, but a caster can stack single-Ability virtues (e.g. Cautious Sorcerer) so a botch — and its aura damage / lab explosion — can never happen; the moment two Abilities are combined (Magic Theory + Magic Lore) those single-Ability safety virtues stop applying. Also ruled: Willhelm may use his Magic-Theory-related virtues when working folk-magic ‘theory’ (the two default to one another, the same fudge used for Valdemar's written magic), with case-by-case exceptions where the heterogeneity of folk traditions means his formal training does not carry over. This is the harvest-in-Divine-auras / ‘prayer-factory’ path discussed for Willhelm + Dietrich at a monastery. Extends the roadmap above; the full mechanical write-up still awaits the sourcebook→DSL conversion.

items.title: What are we preparing for next session?
items.context:
As of the end of Spring 1224 the party is split across two threads — Wilhelm & Éogan making their way home from Ireland, and Dagmar running north from the half-opened Carnac regio (proposed_events p047–p054). This is the GM's working slate of candidate scenes to develop and stage for the next session. The answers so far:

1) WHAT DO WILHELM'S ASSISTANTS BRING BACK — AND COULD IT NEGATE THE HYPOTHESIS? Wilhelm's research assistants were sent west and south over the winter (p049), paid in grain and silver, to gather hedge-tradition material. The night after the parley, the grog FOXGLOVE (scout/rogue, avaricious) quietly took the rowboat back into the Carnac cave alone, dived the cave floor, and smuggled roughly FIVE BAGS of spilled gold aboard — mostly Roman-style coin, priceless — hiding it for herself and lying past Peter (a clean Guile 'caught red-handed' success) about running an errand for Dagmar. THE PROBLEM: this is an unsanctioned theft from a magnitude-10 dragon's hoard, committed the very night Dagmar agreed to run Tormente's peace-errand (t066) and is depending on the dragon's goodwill to pass deeper into the regio (t025). GM REFERENCE (prep 2026-08-08, developing q027 #2) — CONVERTING ROMAN GOLD c.1224. Governing fact: England and NW Europe are on a SILVER standard in 1224 — the silver penny is the coin, and there is NO circulating gold coinage (Henry III's gold penny doesn't come until 1257, and fails). So the Roman coin has no face value anywhere Foxglove can go; it is worth only its WEIGHT in gold as bullion (gold:silver roughly 1:10–1:12), which still makes five bags set-for-life money IF she can convert it without being robbed, taxed, or hanged. Realistic channels: (1) MELT to anonymous bullion at a goldsmith's crucible — destroys the coins' identity, the safest move for a thief, at the cost of the smith's cut; (2) sell/pledge raw gold to a town GOLDSMITH or moneyer (London, York, Newcastle) for silver; (3) JEWISH MONEYLENDERS (London, Lincoln, Norwich, Canterbury — this is pre-1290 expulsion), the era's professional bullion/pledge dealers and the natural discreet fence; (4) ITALIAN / LOMBARD / CAHORSIN bankers, best reached at the FLANDERS FAIRS / BRUGES on the covenant's own trade routes; (5) commission it into WORKED GOODS (rings, brooch, plate) — portable, disguised, origin hidden; (6) the CHURCH / a MONASTERY buying gold for reliquaries, plate, gilding, illumination (also a laundering route via commission or donation). Complications: TREASURE-TROVE law — found hidden gold of unknown owner belongs to the CROWN, so she cannot declare it (honest story = confiscation, dishonest = theft charge), which is exactly why melting appeals; the PROVENANCE problem — a grog flashing Roman aurei in a Stonehenge-Tribunal port is a walking question mark, reputable buyers ask, discreet ones charge for not asking; and weight/portability aboard a 16-crew ship. NOT options: there is NO antiquarian coin-COLLECTOR market yet (numismatic collecting is a Renaissance development, Petrarch a century later); and the coins cannot be spent AS coin north of the Alps. Irony to hold: the best discreet bullion channels (Flanders bankers, the trade net) are the COVENANT'S own — which she cannot use, because she is hiding this from the covenant; laundering pulls her toward the very people who'd recognize the gold. (Where she gets off, whether she's caught, and what she does with it remain the player's calls.)

Update (2026-08-08 session): Advanced. In London, Foxglove could not spend gold in a silver economy; a fence converted only a little (three coins) at a punishing one-for-one (a silver pound per gold piece). She keeps the bulk. She is ALSO wanted elsewhere, so she means to stay close to the covenant for cover while holding the hoard — setting up a reckoning when Dagmar returns to Tormente.

items.title: Éogan's capricorn — a Magic sea-goat as a would-be familiar
items.context:
GM intent (not yet played): on the sea voyage home from Ireland, Éogan discovers a capricorn — a Magic-realm sea-goat (Capricornus) — that singles him out and paces his ship, drawn the same way the small fae gathered on him in Connacht, now escalated to a Might-bearing creature. Intended as a POTENTIAL familiar, not an instant bond: courting it and the binding lab-work are the actual work. Would be the first familiar prospect for any Sjórseiðr magus (directly addresses t037: no PC has bonded a familiar yet), and a payoff for the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' thread. Hooks to settle when activated: whether Éogan courts it, what it wants in return, and how a Magic creature relates to the faerie affinity that drew it. Realm decided: Magic. Placement: the Spring/Summer 1224 voyage home.

DEVELOPED (session prep 2026-08-08, q027 #5). RULINGS: (1) the capricorn's draw to Éogan is INDEPENDENT of any faerie affinity — it is not the same pull as the small fae of t068; a Magic-realm creature coming on its own account. (2) What it wants in exchange for a bond is still OPEN (GM undecided). SIGNATURE SPECIALTY: crossing THRESHOLDS INTO MAGICAL REGIONES — a threshold-creature that can pass (and help its bonded magus pass) regio boundaries, which makes it enormously valuable to a covenant that keeps probing regiones (Carnac, t025/t066, and beyond). MYTHOLOGY to draw on: the sea-goat (goat forequarters, fish/serpent tail) is one of the oldest monsters recorded — the Babylonian 'Goat-Fish' sacred to Enki/Ea, god of fresh water, wisdom, craft and magic; overlaid in Greek myth with Pan's leap into the Nile; and, via Macrobius (a text a learned magus could know), Capricorn is the 'Gate of the Gods,' the solstitial gate through which souls ascend. The consistent motif is LIMINALITY — land and sea, the turn of the year, the boundary of the deep — which is exactly why its specialty is crossing thresholds. CORPUS REFERENCES for building/binding it: familiar Bond + the three Cords (Gold=fewer botch dice, Silver=mind/mental-defence, Bronze=Soak/healing/aging) are in armdef-0.5-full.merged.ttrpg (~line 15519); Magic-creature construction (Might + Realm + Form, Magic Qualities & Inferiorities, Powers costed in Might) and a familiar-scale model are in armdef/0.4/armdef-0.4-bestiary-magical.ttrpg — e.g. the caladrius, Might 14 (Animal). NO ready-made capricorn exists in the export; it is a build-from-scratch. SUGGESTED BUILD (for when Éogan commits): Realm Magic, Might ~12–16, Form Animal or Aquam (bindable by a first-timer but a genuine stretch); Powers themed to a sea-goat and to Éogan's sea magic — breathe/see through water, walk on waves / safe passage, and a regio-threshold-crossing power as its signature; likely Gift of Speech and Second Sight. A tide/weather-sensing angle would also quietly feed the maritime-hedge-tradition motif Wilhelm's thesis still lacks (t009). Directly addresses t037 (no PC magus has bonded a familiar yet).

STATTED (2026-08-08): a playable sheet for the CAPRICORN (Might 14 Magic sea-goat, Threshold-Walker signature) is now in npcs.json — unnamed until Éogan bonds it.

Update (2026-08-08 session): Advanced. Leaving for the ships near Drogheda, Éogan spotted the capricorn at a river-mouth (it favours where salt meets fresh water), took a water sample, and cast a spell to relocate the spot later. Courtship and binding still to come.

items.title: The temporal hedge mage and the brass acorn — a hedge tradition that beat the Limit of Time.
items.context:
Flagged by Wilhelm's assistants on their winter gathering-run west and south (developing q027 #1, session prep 2026-08-08). Among the traditions they turned up is a hedge mage who has genuinely MASTERED TEMPORAL MAGIC — something Hermetic theory cannot do (the Limit of Time is one of the hard walls of the Order's magic). This is both the strongest possible vindication of Wilhelm's core thesis (folk magic reaching where Hermetic theory, having stripped the context out, cannot follow — t019) and a lead worth chasing. He is also the mastered end of the road the Uisneach bird-augury only started down (reading the auspicious signal / the future, p047). THE DEMONSTRATION (a bootstrap paradox): the mage 'came with' the assistants only retroactively — he claims to have attended, then didn't, and told them he had met Wilhelm IN THE FUTURE and given him a BRASS ACORN. Sure enough, Wilhelm finds a brass acorn among his things that he has no memory of packing. The acorn has no point of origin — it exists only because it already exists — which is itself the proof the mage works outside linear time. Tonally it also reassures amid the madness gut-punch: Wilhelm has a future far enough out that he and the mage meet. TO DEVELOP when activated: what the brass acorn actually is (open — pure hook, an Arcane Connection to the mage, or a functional device); the mage's name, tradition, and where in the southwest the assistants found him; and whether he is a rival, a teacher (Insight for the folk system, at a price), or a cautionary example who paid a cost of his own. Possible cross-tie to Dagmar's time-crystal (t018) and his Criamon interest in time.

Update (2026-08-08 session): Confirmed at the table: the memento is a brass ACORN. The assistants relayed the hedge mage's claim of time travel; Wilhelm found the acorn in his luggage, and an Intēllego Vim check found NO magical residue — ruling out a teleport and leaving the temporal claim unexplained.

items.title: Mímormr, the cursed bone-speaking wyrm — Tormente's errand is a jailbreak.
items.context:
Developed from q027 #4 (session prep 2026-08-08), resolving the 'estranged kin-dragon' hook inside t066. MÍMORMR (Mím-, echoing Mímir the severed head of wisdom who speaks knowledge of old things, + ormr, 'serpent') is the kin-dragon dwelling in a sea-cliff cave above the waves off the English NORTHEAST coast (Scarborough / Newcastle, just short of Scotland). It is a SCHOLAR-WYRM: a researcher of ancient things that SPEAKS WITH BONES (interrogates the dead / ancient remains), curious and deeply frustrated, and — critically — it can no longer LEAVE ITS HOLE, because TORMENTE cursed it to stay put many, many years ago.

THE CLAIM: Mímormr styles itself a CHILD OF JÖRMUNGANDR, the greatest magical being that ever was. This is FALSE — but it is true that Jörmungandr existed (Rán may even know a rumor of it; see c022), and Mímormr SINCERELY BELIEVES the descent. Its conviction is motivated reasoning that is genuinely EARNED: questioning ancient bones, it found real traces of Jörmungandr and over-read authentic scholarship into a personal genealogy. A true researcher who reached a false conclusion because it wanted to. The magi therefore cannot easily disprove it — the evidence is real; only the inference is wrong.

THE TRAP: Tormente is a TRICKSTER (mischievous, and can be cruel). The 'reconciliation' errand (t066) is a lie — the Roman crown is the KEY that BREAKS THE CURSE, and Tormente is using Dagmar, a passing Criamon, as an unwitting cat's-paw to loose the thing it caged, keeping its own claws clean. Delivering the crown in good faith earns Dagmar passage deeper into the Carnac regio (t025) at the price of UNBINDING Mímormr — and the party won't know until it's done (open: can they discover the truth in time?).

THE CONSEQUENCE: freed, Mímormr becomes an ENVIRONMENTAL THREAT to the region — not necessarily hostile to the magi, but catastrophic to be near. GM flavor to pick/stack when activated: a sea-wyrm whose passage floods coasts and sinks hulls; a bone-speaker whose curiosity cracks open barrows and rouses the restless dead; storm-weather in its wake (fits the Carnac regio reading 'more Auram than Aquam'); or an aura/vis-draining apex predator that blights the stretch of coast it settles on. REAL-WORLD ANCHOR: the English northeast is worm-legend country (the Lambton Worm, the Sockburn Worm, the Laidly Worm of Spindleston Heugh) — a loose Mímormr can SEED or BECOME the origin of those Northumbrian dragon-legends.

TO DEVELOP when activated: Mímormr's Might / statblock (Tormente is magnitude-10 and was strong enough to cage it — set Mímormr's relative power; a Magic-realm dragon); the exact release mechanics of the crown; whether and how the party can learn the truth before acting; and whether Foxglove's unsanctioned hoard theft (c026) tangles in. Cross-ref t066, t025, c022, c026, t018.

STATBLOCK BASIS (2026-08-08): build Mímormr on POLYMATHES, THE DRACONIC LIBRARIAN (Realms of Power: Magic p.76; present in the merged corpus) — a dragon whose avarice is for KNOWLEDGE, not gold, hoarding rare and ancient lore. Base chassis to keep: Might 41 (Animal), Size +7, Int +5 / Pre +8 / Str +12 / Sta +8; Essential Flaw Avaricious (major) + Inquisitive; the scholar kit (Educated, Arcane Lore, Second Sight, Gift of Speech, Magic Lore 6 'ancient magic', Philosophiae 6, Artes Liberales, Latin/Greek/Arabic); the InMe 'Peering Into the Mortal Mind' power (reads the mind of anyone it can see); Poisonous Blood (CrAq); and the telling 9 Intellego vis in the heart. Note Might 41 sits BELOW Tormente (build Tormente on STELLATUS, the Dragon — Might 50, MR 50 = magnitude-10), which is why Tormente could cage it. ADAPTATIONS to make it Mímormr: (1) hoard = ancient BONES and relics, not books; (2) replace Polymathes's Master of Illusion focus with a 'SPEAKS WITH BONES' Intellego focus (Corpus/Mentem, interrogating the dead) — the Intellego heart-vis fits a diviner exactly; (3) the false Jörmungandr-descent belief falls straight out of Magic Lore 6 + bone-divination (real traces of Jörmungandr, over-read into a personal genealogy — genuine scholarship, wrong inference, so the magi can't easily disprove it); (4) reskin the squat golden mountain-lizard into a long serpentine SEA-WYRM in the Scarborough/Newcastle sea-cliff cave, keeping Poisonous Blood (Aquam) and optionally reskinning Fiery Breath to a storm/brine breath to match the Carnac regio's Auram lean; (5) the curse ('cannot leave its hole') is an EXTERNAL binding Tormente laid, broken by the Roman crown — not an innate stat. Freed, its Size +7 bulk and restless curiosity are the regional threat (sunk hulls, flooded coasts, barrows cracked for bones, storm-wake).

STATTED (2026-08-08): full playable sheets for TORMENTE (on the Stellatus chassis, Might 50) and MÍMORMR (silver/aquamarine sea-wyrm, Might 41, briny-north-wind breath) are now in npcs.json as 'entity' statblocks.

Update (2026-08-08 session): The reveal played out. Mímormr is a giant silver-and-aquamarine worm who sincerely claims descent from Jörmungandr and 'speaks with the bones of the dead'; Tormente disputes the ancestry and called its deeds wicked. Delivering Tormente's crown broke the binding and FREED it — it means to finish work here, then head east into the North Sea to seek a relative's bones. Now a loose threat (see c027). The binding proved non-Hermetic (see q029).

dossier.summary: Valdemar's Isle-of-Man build — the player's original notes, followed by the Storyteller's decisions

sections.heading: The player's original notes (verbatim)
sections.body:
So Valdemar is building a comfortable little manor equivalent for his friends to Winter in, and it includes a very impressive laboratory for him to make use of during the cold months where sailing, raiding, and trading is difficult.

During most every other part of the year, Valdemar would rather be out sailing, learning from real people. If nothing else, he's learning languages from his fellow sailors, so he doesn't need to lean on his magic to speak to anyone he wants to talk to.

So, trying to get an idea of the Size that Valdemar could build his Viking-Style Longhouse Laboratory (with some 12th Century upgrades, like more solid stone walls, proper chimneys for ventilation, and, you know, these newfangled things called windows), I get a wild range of estimates for a simple question (How big were they?)

This is the largest one the internet knows of at about 6,000 square feet. https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/archaeologists-find-one-of-largest-viking-longhouses-in-scandinavia-180979177/

This matters because the Size of the Structure is a primary source of Virtue Points before I can develop its Refinement (which is a trait that requires my Magical Theory to improve, which will come with time) - there aren't a ton of flaws I'd be willing to incorporate right out of the gate. If Valdemar built a 6,000 Square Foot Longhouse, that would be worth about 15 Virtue Points. Is that unreasonably huge, or is that simply going to be costly/take longer/etc.

I'm also researching the comparable sizes of contemporary Medieval Manors, for comparison and to get an idea of what architects of the day would be capable of, because Valdemar has by this point seen a lot of contemporary houses and knows what design elements that he wants to incorporate, and they ranged from about 1,000 to 5,000 square feet depending on the wealth of the lord, so pushing that high end with a traditionally long and wide design doesn't seem completely unreasonable, at least to me.

I will also need to know how Upkeep works. I may opt for a smaller lab because of the Safety Factor - a Big Lab can be dangerous - and some of the things I would like to add increase Upkeep.

EDIT: Nevermind, I found it in the "Expenses" Section, and figured out what it will run me to keep it up. It will all be in the plan.

On doing further research, I found the name for the "Manor" that Valdemar is assembling for the Covenant:

Noatun

Its meaning is the "Place of Ships" or "Ship Enclosure", it was the Hall of Njord, whose unhappy marriage to Skadi created the seasons as they moved between his house by the sea and hers in the mountains. So that is the name that Valdemar is going to give the whole Manor. I'm still working on what he will call his Laboratory / Home (though it is likely the "Home" Part of the Hall will be separate from the "Lab" Part, for Safety reasons)

He calls the entire seaside harbor area that he has acquired to build the manor "Ránargarðr" - Ran's Garden.

Undrahöll - The Name of the Hall that includes his Laboratory.

It means "Hall of Wonders" in Old Norse. It also includes living quarters for himself and Rán, though with clear separation between the Living Quarters and the Lab.

I have some questions about Specializations. I gather every bonus that impacts my Lab Total will add to any workings I do in the Lab. I can only have the Lab enhance 2 Activities and 4 Hermetic Magical Categories (2 Techniques and 2 Forms, or more Forms with less Techniques.)

There are so many types of things that I could do with it that it will be hard to choose!

I'm leaning towards Spells and Items, and my logic being that Spells are working the Deidne Style Hermetic Magic - practicing that in an Antechamber is currently what I'm thinking - while Items and Enchantments speak to the Viktir Rune-Carving, unless I can use the Spells specialization on both. Which is my question - Runes are both spells and objects, so do I use Items, Spells, or both to enhance my Lab Total in RE: preparing Rune Magic.

++++

Alright, I have the wishlist compiled:

Valdemar's Hall of Wonders (Laboratory built inside a modified Viking Longhouse)

Undrahöll - The Name of the Hall that includes his Laboratory. It means "Hall of Wonders" in Old Norse. It also includes living quarters for himself and Rán, though with clear separation between the Living Quarters and the Lab.

He calls the entire seaside harbor area that he has acquired to build the manor "Ránargarðr" - Ran's Garden. Which may well become the name of the village that arises around the main hall.

The Main Hall is called Nóatún, after Njord's Seaside Hall. It means "Place of Ships" or "Ship Enclosure" - appropriate for where the Coven Winters.

Laboratory Characteristics:

Size: 13 (Use what you need) + Refinement (0)

[Construction Costs are One Pound per 2 Points of Laboratory (See Upkeep, below) - Valdemar opted for Superior Construction, though, so it's actually 1 for 1 - 60 Mythic Pounds. Valdemar better have a good Trading/Raiding Season.]

Refinement: Stuck at 0 for now.

sections.heading: The Storyteller's decisions & rulings
sections.body:
Ruled 2026-08-15, after walking the build against the Covenants lab rules.

— VIKTIR & THE LABORATORY —

Viktir rune-workings function as SPELLS: in place of Technique + Form they use the relevant rune Abilities in the Lab Total. So learning/inventing a rune-spell-effect is the "Spells" lab activity — enhanced by the Antechamber's +3 Spells and by General Quality.

Imbuing an object with a rune is a DISTINCT activity, handled exactly as enchanting an object with a spell: the "Items" activity — enhanced by the +3 Items (Forge + Running Water + Superior Tools) and by General Quality. Both of Valdemar's chosen Activity specializations (Spells AND Items) are therefore load-bearing for his own practice, which is why picking both is coherent rather than scattered.

General Quality (+1) adds to every Lab Total except Teaching and Texts (Covenants p.110). Art specializations add only to workings that use that Art — so Rego/Aquam help his Diedne Hermetic magic, not his rune-work (unless a slot is pointed at a rune; see below).

Effective lab bonuses:
 • learn/invent a rune-spell-effect ....... +4 (Spells +3, GQ +1)
 • imbue an object with a rune ............ +4 (Items +3, GQ +1)
 • invent a Diedne Rego Hermetic spell .... +5 (Rego +1, Spells +3, GQ +1)
 • invent a Diedne Aquam Hermetic spell ... +5 (Aquam +1, Spells +3, GQ +1)
 • enchant a device (Hermetic) ............ +4 (Items +3, GQ +1)

— SPECIALIZATIONS: PLAYER'S CHOICE OFFERED —

Because runes are a viktir magus's functional "Arts," the lab's four Art-specialization slots may be pointed at RUNES instead of Hermetic Techniques/Forms. The player may choose, per slot, rune-based or Technique/Form-based specialization:
 • A terrain/purpose feature grants the rune associated with it — e.g. the seaside Idyllic Surroundings can grant Laguz (the water-rune) in place of Aquam.
 • A free-choice feature (Dedicated Building) may pick either a rune or a Hermetic Art (currently Rego).
He stays under the 2-Activities + 4-Arts cap either way (he uses only 2 Art slots).

— THE BUILD, RATIFIED —

Size 13 — 9 points spent on features, 2 Empty holding 4 points in reserve for future Refinement. Legal; the cost is paid in Safety and silver.
Safety 0 (features +9 − occupied size 9). Superior Construction doubles the outlay: 100£ to build (100 lab points × ½£, doubled).
General Quality +1; Aesthetics +11 (≈55-point Rune-Master reputation); Health 0; Warping 0.
Refinement 0 for now (capped at Magic Theory 3; rises with study).

— UPKEEP: CORRECTED TO 4 —

Dedicated Building's +1 Upkeep counts, so Upkeep = 4 (not 3) = 100 upkeep points. Per the Points of Laboratories table (Covenants), yearly maintenance = points × season-use multiplier ÷ 10:
 • ≤1 season/yr: ×0.5 → 5£/yr
 • 2 seasons/yr: ×1.0 → 10£/yr
 • 3-4 seasons/yr: ×1.5 → 15£/yr
Valdemar works the lab mostly in Winter (one season), so baseline upkeep is 5£/yr.

— CONSTRUCTION: CORRECTED TO 100£ (2026-08-15) —

The build cost tracks the same lab-points total that drives upkeep. Correcting Upkeep 3 → 4 raised that total 60 → 100 points, so construction rises with it: 100 points × ½£, doubled by Superior Construction = 100£. (The player's original notes above read 60£ — the earlier 60-point / Upkeep-3 figure.) Confirmed against the Covenants conversion (titterpig-dsl-arm5e): the Points of Laboratories table sets Upkeep +3 = 60 and +4 = 100; the build cost is one pound per two points, doubled by Superior Construction. Covenants' own worked example — raising Upkeep +2→+4 (a +70-point jump) costs 35£ — matches exactly.

— THE NAMES (CANON) —

Ránargarðr ("Rán's Garden") — the seaside harbour holding acquired for the manor; likely the name of the village that grows around it.
Nóatún ("Place of Ships," Njord's seaside hall) — the covenant's main Hall on the Isle of Man, where the coven Winters.
Undrahöll ("Hall of Wonders") — the hall housing Valdemar's laboratory and his and Rán's living quarters, living space kept separate from the lab for Safety.

— PENDING —

Final specialization picks (rune vs Technique/Form, per slot) are the player's to make.
Construction (60£) and upkeep are funded through the raiding/trading seasons and booked in the covenant ledger; hold the actual build seasons until the specs are locked.

items.title: Valdemar's title to the Isle of Man — the owed favour, the fief, and the Christian lie.
items.context:
GM note 2026-08-15. Valdemar has quietly secured right and title to the Ránargarðr holding on the Isle of Man through a private arrangement the covenant knows nothing about: a big favour done for the current Norse Ruler of Man, a down payment made in goods or services, and title received in writing. He wants to hold the land in fact, not merely by sword-right, and to keep the local potentate a friend — though that ruler's ENEMIES are fair game. The open question is the FORM of the obligation — an Oath of Fealty (which Valdemar would rather avoid) versus a promise of specific service — and the standing DEBT it leaves him owing, which the GM may call in at any time.

Next-session beat (scene s14): the fief is granted — potentially as a proper feudal fief — but Valdemar must LIE and profess himself a Christian to receive and hold it. That deception stacks on his hidden House Diedne lineage (t078): a pagan viktir magus, secretly Diedne, now also perjuring his faith to a Christian-facing authority to hold mundane land openly. Rich exposure if it ever unravels.

Longer arc (player-flagged, optional): Valdemar may later move to own the Isle outright — unseating the local lord with the complicity of the King of Norway — if the other magi take interest.

Settlement plan: recruit grog families first, then island/mainland settlers wanting new farmland to clear, then other pirates and their families; a Norse 'bailiff' to run the place while Valdemar raids and trades; justice dispensed by Valdemar as local lord when in port; and a winter Althing for community decisions — a Viking fjord-town in the making around Nóatún. The player's full hand-off is in the dossier below.

Rules aside (the player's question — 'no rules about Hermetics ruling land openly in our Tribunal, right?'): there is no blanket Hermetic ban on owning or ruling mundane land, but the Oath's clause against interfering with mundanes and thereby bringing ruin on one's sodales is the lever a quaesitor would reach for — openly ruling a fief is deep mundane entanglement. Whether it crosses the line is a Tribunal call, and this border sea-covenant already runs on unusual mundane latitude (see the Normandy 'Mundane Goods Are Fair Game' custom). Plausible — but it widens his exposure. Cross-ref t079 (the manor & lab), s13/s14, and t078 (Confluensis and the Diedne secret).

dossier.summary: Valdemar's Isle-of-Man title — the player's hand-off (the favour, the fief, the settlement)

sections.heading: The player's hand-off (verbatim)
sections.body:
There is probably a side story somewhere that the Covenant doesn't know about wherein Valdemar did a big favor for the current (Norse) Ruler of Man to gain right and title to the land.

Valdemar wants to own the property in fact as well as by sword right, and doesn't want the local potentate as an enemy (though enemies of that person, well, those guys are fair game). There are lots of ways a Wizard can be of use to a Warlord. Whatever agreement they came to, Valdemar has at least made the down payment in goods or services and received in writing the title to the property. This can involve an Oath of Fealty, though that would not be Valdemar's preference. He would rather promise specific service in exchange for the right to the land. (Valdemar might one day decide he just wants to own the Isle outright, and may develop plans to unseat the local lord at the behest of or with the complicity of the King of Norway. This might be a future plotline if the others take interest too. No rules about Hermetics NOT ruling land openly exist in our Tribunal, right?)

This presumed debt/promise of support/owed service/favor/etc. is a complication I am handing you to feel free to reference / make use of at any point future.

In terms of population, I'd first look to recruit the families of our Grogs, then local inhabitants from the island or mainland wanting new farmlands to clear, then other pirates and their families. Valdemar will appoint the Norse equivalent of a Bailiff to manage the settlement while he's out doing what Norsemen do, will dispense justice as the local lord when in town, and he will convene a traditional Althing in the Winter to deal with community concerns and make big decisions.

Basically, this settlement is a Viking Fjord Town in the making at the moment.

items.title: Valdemar seeks fellow viktir magi — now looking to Hibernia and Scotland.
items.context: GM note 2026-08-10. Valdemar (viktir tradition — Norse rune-song magic; see magi.json) wants to widen his search for other viktir magi into HIBERNIA and SCOTLAND — looking for viktir experts while trading through Ireland and Scotland. This continues the quest begun in the north, where he asked around for another viktir magus and was pointed to Þóra Ketilsdóttir the Bone-Keeper, a maga hermit in a northern fjord, from whom he learned three rune-songs (mechanically summa for study; see the Chronicle). What viktir practitioners exist in Ireland or Scotland — and whether they read as teachers, rivals, or recruits — is open. Leans on the party's existing Hibernian footprint (the Cruachan magi Gráinne & Tadhg, the Uisneach / Connacht Gifted-child delivery custom).

brugesRoster.title: Bruges — Cast in Reserve
brugesRoster.note: Mundane NPCs the GM prepared for the covenant's home port. None have been used in play yet (per the GM's own notes) — pull from here rather than inventing a new face when a Bruges scene needs one.

entries.name: Anselmo ex Bonisagus
entries.title: Hermetic Scholar in Disguise
entries.note: Posing as a mundane doctor, Anselmo studies the northern humors and arcane sickness. Secretly writing a treatise on magical bloodlines. Keeps a raven that speaks riddles in Latin.

entries.name: Benedictus of Jerbiton
entries.title: Jerbiton Magus, "the Silver Tongue of Southampton"
entries.note: A polished, silver-haired magus whose sanctum lies just beyond Southampton's old Roman walls, doubling as a salon for artists, merchants, and minor nobles. Believes beauty is a form of moral truth. Has taken an interest in Stijntje Kuiper — courting her with raven-borne letters and gifts, and an open invitation to visit his library-laced sanctum "for a season or two." Behind the charm: he wants to build a salon of magical minds loyal to him.

entries.name: Bertrand du Lys
entries.title: Exiled Knight of Hainaut
entries.note: A brooding swordsman and foreign noble fallen on hard times. Lives above a fletcher's shop. Rumored to have dueled a Duke's son. Possibly looking for redemption — or revenge.

entries.name: Boudewijn van der Voorde
entries.title: Captain of the Watch
entries.note: Grizzled ex-soldier, loyal to the guilds, hates paperwork. Struggles balancing leniency toward the poor against brutality toward outlanders. Drinks too much but knows the city inside out. Could be swayed with principle — or silver.

entries.name: Brother Joost
entries.title: Mad Anchorite
entries.note: Lives walled into a cell behind a chapel, speaking only once per day through a tiny window. On Saint's Days he speaks in rhymes that often predict events — or deaths. People leave coins and questions on slips of parchment.

entries.name: Brother Savin
entries.title: Clerical Advocate for the Bishopric
entries.note: Sent from Tournai to monitor the city's moral climate. Walks the line between Church authority and local law. Often appears at trials involving sorcery or "unnatural behavior." May be an agent of the Dominican Order — or something darker.

entries.name: Brother Tomás
entries.title: Hospitaller at the Abbey of St. Andrew
entries.note: A quiet, Spanish-born monk with a sharp memory and gentle touch. His abbey holds records of river shipments and sick travelers, and he occasionally sees prophetic dreams.

entries.name: Canon Gilles de Roon
entries.title: Political Preacher
entries.note: Stern-faced and ambitious, delivers fire-and-brimstone sermons against foreign entanglements and "unclean miracles." Suspected of collusion with Brabant's envoys. Keeps a locked chest of anonymous donations in silver.

entries.name: Cilene of Criamon
entries.title: Wandering Mystic
entries.note: A heavily tattooed woman with a strange cadence and no visible luggage. Preaches at corners and weeps when the moon wanes. Her cryptic words hold clues to regio entrances.

entries.name: Colette-with-the-Bell
entries.title: Street Courtesan and Spy
entries.note: Young and charming, with a silver bell on her ankle. Trades rumors between nobles, sailors, and thieves. Claims to have seen "the pretty one with the lute" thrown into a laundry cart by cloaked men.

entries.name: Deacon Renard of Cambrai
entries.title: Visiting Inquisitor's Aide
entries.note: Thin, beady-eyed, always watching. Travels under the banner of a Church investigation into heretical activities. Claims he's here about Cathars, but shows keen interest in "unlicensed healers and unnatural weather."

entries.name: Dirk “Two-Fathoms” van Velsen
entries.title: Lame Dockhand
entries.note: Lost a leg to a kraken — or so he says. Spends his time carving obscene mermaids and watching the tide. Claims he saw Valerian dragged aboard a barge with black sails.

entries.name: Etienne the Dustwalker
entries.title: Redcap
entries.note: Thin, bone-pale, and always dusty. Moves between covenants disguised as a beggar. Delivers messages and smuggles magical items through Bruges under the guise of wine shipments.

entries.name: Father Willem
entries.title: Old Harbormaster Priest
entries.note: Tends a shrine near the docks to St. Nicholas. Grizzled and fond of gin, but devout. Hears more confessions than anyone in Bruges, and keeps a coded book of what he learns — supposedly to "pray more effectively."

entries.name: Francois Malvoisin
entries.title: Antiquarian and Book Dealer
entries.note: Gnarled like the driftwood he collects, hoards texts and scraps of lore in his riverside shop. May have connections to Hermetic redcaps but denies all knowledge of magic.

entries.name: Greet of the Orchard
entries.title: Elder Sex Worker Turned Healer
entries.note: Once a famed courtesan, now runs an herbal bathhouse for women. Offers charms and quiet advice. Knows who's coming and going in the pleasure district and keeps coded symbols on her entry door each night.

entries.name: Hendrick Lamoen
entries.title: Night Watchman and Rat-Catcher
entries.note: Unkempt, paranoid, always armed with a lantern and spiked cudgel. Claims he's seen a "man with mirrored eyes" walking the rooftops at midnight.

entries.name: Ingrid of the Mire
entries.title: Fae-Touched Midwife
entries.note: Her eyes reflect moonlight even during the day. Always knows when someone is pregnant — and sometimes what the child will be. Fears "a boy born with iron in his mouth."

entries.name: Isko of Reval
entries.title: Runaway Baltic Sailor
entries.note: Towering and soft-spoken, speaks broken Flemish and better Latin. Trying to disappear in Bruges after stealing a precious charm from his former captain. Superstitious and wary of magic.

entries.name: Jakob d’Ypres
entries.title: Rival Dock Foreman
entries.note: Gruff and territorial. Hates magic, hates taxes, hates poets. Recently fired a man for "asking too many questions about river routes to Dinant." Keeps a ledger under his bed — some pages removed.

entries.name: Jan de Brakel
entries.title: Guild Master of the Carpenters
entries.note: Burly and thick-fingered, sawdust permanently in his beard. Secretly sheltering a Tytalus apprentice who fled his master.

entries.name: Judicratix Margriet van Heule
entries.title: Chief Schepen
entries.note: Sharp-tongued, always veiled, entirely incorruptible (or so she insists). Keeps notes in a personal cipher. Jurisdiction over property disputes, thefts, and "disruptions of civic peace." Suspects something unnatural in the canals.

entries.name: Klaas the Candle-Boy
entries.title: Lantern Escort and Listener
entries.note: Hired to walk clients home safely at night, mostly silent and watchful. Exceptional memory for faces and footsteps. Recently saw someone matching Valerian's description leaving with "two monks with hard hands."

entries.name: Lady Joan of Constantinople
entries.title: Countess of Flanders
entries.note: Elegant and intense, rules from Ghent, but her envoys keep a sharp eye on Bruges. Rarely seen in person, but every major noble in Bruges is either trying to support or subvert her. Secretly seeking magical aid to secure her lineage — perhaps a Hermetic opportunity.

entries.name: Lady Ysabel van Aardenburg
entries.title: Merchant Matriarch
entries.note: Sharp-witted and impeccably dressed in Flemish silks, controls a powerful wool and dye trading house. Polite but fiercely protective of Bruges' autonomy from foreign nobles.

entries.name: Lisette the Bold
entries.title: Madam of the Gilded Fig
entries.note: Raven-haired and iron-willed, runs the most luxurious brothel in Bruges. Her girls are trained in song, wit, and secrets. Valerian once performed here — Lisette keeps a lock of his hair.

entries.name: Madame Lieve
entries.title: Owner of the Crimson Duck Inn
entries.note: Witty, middle-aged, always one step ahead. Her tavern is a crossroads for gossip, illicit deals, and out-of-town couriers. Knows how to listen without seeming to.

entries.name: Maeva the Windkeeper
entries.title: Barge Captain
entries.note: A Breton woman with a raven tattoo and hair in iron rings. Sails under no banner and fears no storm. Rumors say her ship can sail even with torn sails — and that she once kissed a selkie.

entries.name: Magister Lambert
entries.title: City Scribe & Notary
entries.note: Impeccably organized, ink-stained fingers, bland expression. Quietly records all disputes, taxes, and legal matters. May have access to intercepted letters or Duke Brabant's agents' missives.

entries.name: Marthe aux Cendres
entries.title: Local Wise Woman (Cunning Folk)
entries.note: Lives in a peat-hut on the edge of the marshes. People claim she speaks with ghosts and cures madness. The local clergy are suspicious, but none dare move against her openly.

entries.name: Pieter van Cleeff
entries.title: Canal Boatman and Informant
entries.note: Wiry and grinning, knows the waterways better than anyone. Trades in rumors, contraband, and the occasional missing person.

entries.name: Ragna “the Guilder”
entries.title: Fence & Secret Broker
entries.note: A large, laughing woman with scarred hands and fine clothes. Brokers secrets as easily as smuggled goods. Keeps a circle of loyal thugs and a hidden tunnel beneath her shop.

entries.name: Roeland the Roper
entries.title: Ropemaker and Smuggler
entries.note: Broad-shouldered and cheerfully profane. His ropes are prized by sailors — but some include knotted symbols only certain buyers understand. Secretly a courier for Etienne the Dustwalker.

entries.name: Sir Rombout de Noyon
entries.title: Commander of the Castellan's Guard
entries.note: Noble-born, self-righteous, disdainful of commoners. Trains his men like soldiers, tolerates no insubordination, and has "special permission" from Duke Brabant to act outside Bruges' charter. May be directly tied to Valerian's disappearance.

entries.name: Sister Annelies
entries.title: Abbess of the Veiled Heart
entries.note: Warm but commanding, tends to fallen women and abandoned children. Known for sharp negotiation with the city's merchants. Whispers say she once healed a blind beggar — who immediately fled the city.

entries.name: Tomkin “The Little Lord”
entries.title: Effeminate Companion
entries.note: Dressed in velvet and blush, caters to nobles and scholars alike. Collects poetry, keeps a diary disguised as a songbook. Knows Valerian personally — calls him "heart-sigh." Will trade knowledge for a new gown.

entries.name: Willem de Lichtervelde
entries.title: Court Scribe & Informant
entries.note: Thin, quiet, invisible at most gatherings. Records confessions, trial outcomes, civic pronouncements. Known to pass quiet bribes to ensure charges "go missing." Might help the players — for the right cause or price.

entries.name: Baron Arnulf van Maele
entries.title: Stoic Elder Noble, House van Maele
entries.note: Proud, frost-haired, and blunt. Supports Bruges' civic independence and funds local hospitals and churches. Loyal to Countess Joan. Believes in alliances with Hermetic magi, but keeps it very discreet.

entries.name: Sir Odo van Aerschot
entries.title: Knight and Diplomat, House van Aerschot (Brabantine loyalists)
entries.note: Young, well-dressed, venomously polite. Suspected to be behind several disappearances in Bruges — including Valerian's. Maintains a suspiciously large household guard and discreetly meets with Church figures.

entries.name: Lady Ermengarde van Ruddervoorde
entries.title: Dowager with Ambition, House van Ruddervoorde
entries.note: Wears silks from Outremer, drinks heavy wine, speaks in riddles. Hosts salons where songs, lies, and truths blur. Once patronized Valerian, and may still mourn his absence.

entries.name: Diederik van Aardenburg
entries.title: Young Lord-in-Waiting, House van Aardenburg
entries.note: Hot-headed and eager to prove himself. Dabbles in fencing, philosophy, and potentially Hermetic ideas. Might become an ally or pawn depending on the party's approach. Kin to Lady Ysabel van Aardenburg.

seaFae.title: Sea Fae Bestiary
seaFae.note: Deep-sea fae, organized by ocean depth. Meant to feel alien and incomprehensible the deeper you go — GM reference for anything involving the covenant's fae/merfolk entanglements (Rán, Ka'wa'ill, Marina).

poem.title: The Depths Hold Many Names
stanzas:
The winds at play on silvered tides,
The gilded lords of mist and spray.
They dance and weave, they trick and smile,
But do not trust their fleeting guile.

Below them dine the drowned kings
and with them sailors lost at sea
Their table welcomes every guest
Should forfeit they a memory.

The weavers sing, and braid their net
To bind the lost and keep the dead
A tangled gift, a silken grave,
Swim not where memory calls the wave.

Amidst the dark a flicker's gleam,
A gentle voice, a waking dream.
Follow soft and follow bright,
And never, never see the light.

False currents pull where maps have lied,
A hungry path, the shifting tide.
One moment west, one moment none,
And when you turn, your home is gone.

The Molt-Sworn shed, their shells remain,
Hollow things with clicking frames.
An aura of them may abide
But nothing in them true resides

Drifters glow with absent thought,
Long tendrils trace what time forgot.
To take your breath, to taste the past,
And leave you sinking, thoughtless, glass.

The beggars bound deep whisper low,
In chains of tides they twist and flow.
They call for hands, they beg for keys,
Bound for cause, eternally,

Wells of black a gaping maw,
To them foolish prey they draw
They do not move, they do not wait,
But pull you down to share their fate.

The cold gods dream beyond all years,
They watch through waves, they dream your fears.
They see not flesh, they hear no cry,
A inhuman sympathy belied

Light and shadow, each must stay,
Far from where the still ones lay.
For what sleeps deep beneath the tide,
Knows no master, spares no guide.

zones.name: Epipelagic Zone (0–200m) — The Surface Lords
zones.description: These fae interact with sailors, islands, and storms — still comprehensible, but capricious.

entities.name: The Drowned Kings
entities.description: Ghostly faerie rulers of lost ships who command floating graveyards of wrecks. See the ocean as their kingdom of the dead; their courts hold banquets of drowned sailors.

entities.name: Wave Riders
entities.description: Horse-like fae that gallop across the surface of the water, sometimes carrying ships or luring them into unreachable faerie regios.

zones.name: Mesopelagic Zone (200–1000m) — The Sunken Courts
zones.description: Half-visible, bioluminescent, aware of the world above but bound to the twilight below.

entities.name: The Netweavers
entities.description: Living, sentient fishing nets that ensnare not just fish but souls and memories. Sailors who drown in them live on as whispering ghosts in their fibers.

entities.name: The Flickerlights
entities.description: Predatory fae resembling dancing lights in the darkness. Trick divers into following them into deep trenches where they vanish forever.

entities.name: The False Currents
entities.description: Shapeless fae that mimic trade winds and currents, leading ships off course into forgotten, unmapped waters.

zones.name: Bathypelagic Zone (1000–4000m) — The Abyssal Emperors
zones.description: No sunlight reaches here. Massive, ancient, slow-moving; their consciousness stretches over centuries.

entities.name: The Molt-Sworn
entities.description: Crab-like fae that continuously molt and regrow, leaving behind empty, animated husks of themselves. Trade skins and identities — some say magi who bargain with them can shed their age, for a price.

entities.name: The Dream Drifters
entities.description: Jellyfish-like fae that weave dreams into their tendrils, consuming memories and thoughts instead of flesh. The deeper you go, the more likely you are to forget why you came.

entities.name: The Leviathan-Bound
entities.description: Prisoner-gods of the deep, shackled by unknowable entities. Some escaped from Faerie, some from Hell — they'll promise anything to be freed.

zones.name: Abyssopelagic Zone (4000–6000m) — The Sleeping Ones
zones.description: Barely awake, existing in vast timeless slumber — but if disturbed, could shift entire oceans.

entities.name: The Black Wells
entities.description: Entire trenches that are actually immense fae-beings, their bodies forming undersea canyons and ridges. Those who swim too close hear voices calling them deeper.

entities.name: The Cold Gods
entities.description: Massive, slow-moving creatures entirely wrapped in darkness, sensing only by vibration and thought. See through time rather than space, and might react to the magi's search for vis long before it happens.

zones.name: Hadal Zone (6000m+) — The Unfathomable
zones.description: Barely fae at all — concepts of hunger, pressure, and stillness given form.

entities.name: Jörmungandr's Corpse
entities.description: Off the coast of Norway, in the deepest part of the sea, lies the roughly 27km-long corpse of Jörmungandr, long since transformed into a kind of magical petroleum saturated with vis. Anything sapient below the mesopelagic is a stretch to assume, but this is the exception.

entities.name: The Last Maw
entities.description: A being that does not move, yet its mouth is always open. Devours the shadows of those who pass; those who lose their shadow eventually cease to exist.

entities.name: The Final Pact
entities.description: A faerie deeper than any known depth, which will grant any wish in exchange for something you don't yet know you have.

criamonRiddles.title: Criamon Riddles & Answers
criamonRiddles.note: A shallow and a deep answer for each of the 15 Hermetic Arts, in Criamon mystery-cult style — a reusable puzzle bank for Cilene of Criamon, or any other Criamon magus. Dagmar's own answers to four of these (Imaginem, Herbam, Vim, Auram) are on his character sheet, and don't always match the "deep" answer given here — that's intentional; every Criamon magus reasons their own way in.

entries.label: “I Create”
entries.riddle: From where does the sun rise when the world is shrouded in endless night?
entries.shallow: From the east, as it always has.
entries.deep: From within. Light is not given, but remembered.

entries.label: “I Perceive”
entries.riddle: If a silent man whispers a secret, who has heard it?
entries.shallow: No one, for he made no sound.
entries.deep: The silence itself holds the secret, for knowledge is not always spoken.

entries.label: “I Transform”
entries.riddle: A serpent eats its tail, becoming itself again. Did it ever change?
entries.shallow: Yes, it changed as it consumed itself.
entries.deep: No, for it was always itself. Change is only the forgetting of what was already true.

entries.label: “I Destroy”
entries.riddle: When a shadow is swallowed by the night, where does it go?
entries.shallow: It vanishes, for there is no light to cast it.
entries.deep: It becomes the night, for absence is but another form of presence.

entries.label: “I Control”
entries.riddle: Who commands the river: the mountain that births it, the valley that holds it, or the sea that swallows it?
entries.shallow: The sea, for all rivers flow to it.
entries.deep: None and all. The river commands itself, moving by nature, yet shaped by all.

entries.riddle: A bird trapped in a cage and a fish trapped in water — who is more free?
entries.shallow: The fish, for it is where it belongs.
entries.deep: Neither, for each is confined by the limits of their understanding.

entries.label: “Water”
entries.riddle: A drop of water in the ocean and the ocean in a drop. Which is greater?
entries.shallow: The ocean, for it is vast and mighty.
entries.deep: Neither, for the ocean is nothing but many drops.

entries.label: “Air”
entries.riddle: I built a house of wind, and it held my breath. Why did it collapse when I exhaled?
entries.shallow: Wind is nothing. It cannot be shaped nor hold anything.
entries.deep: The house was real, but I no longer believed in it. My breath gave it form, my doubt destroyed it.

entries.label: “Body”
entries.riddle: My finger rotted, but I am still whole. Whose body is this?
entries.shallow: It is your body still. Parts may fail, but the self remains.
entries.deep: No part is mine, only borrowed. The body is a story the soul tells, and it forgets its lines.

entries.label: “Plant”
entries.riddle: A tree that stands for a hundred years and a flower that blooms for a day — which has lived longer?
entries.deep: The flower, for it knew no waiting.

entries.label: “Fire”
entries.riddle: What is the shape of fire?
entries.shallow: It has no shape, for it moves as it pleases.
entries.deep: It is the shape of change, for it devours all yet leaves nothing behind.

entries.label: “Image”
entries.riddle: If I wear a mask and none see beneath it, do I still exist?
entries.shallow: Yes, for I am here beneath the mask.
entries.deep: No, for I am only what others perceive.

entries.label: “Mind”
entries.riddle: A thought never spoken and a word never heard — do they have meaning?
entries.shallow: No, for meaning is given by those who receive it.
entries.deep: Yes, for meaning is not in the telling but in the knowing.

entries.label: “Earth”
entries.riddle: A stone rests unmoved for a thousand years. Was it patient, or merely forgotten?
entries.shallow: It was forgotten, for stone does not think or feel.
entries.deep: It was patient, for in stillness it remembered the shape of the world before motion.

entries.label: “Power”
entries.shallow: Nothing, for the infinite has no bounds.
entries.deep: Itself, for infinity is a circle, ever turning upon its own path.
